newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products hold ground underpinned by crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products hold ground underpinned by crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all steady to a touch firmer on Tuesday, traders said.
Gasoline markets were steady to firmer tracking crude and products futures. Most players are thought to have covered short term commitments ahead of the Easter weekend holidays.
Supplies were expected to tighten with refiners looking mostly covered combined with warmer weather that may create some extra demand from drivers.
"The market tracked the losses on crude on Monday but the underlying sentiment is bullish and those losses have been reversed today," one trader said.
Prompt Eurograde cargoes valued around $202 cif Med.

Naphtha was steady but with firmer crude and fresh interest from the Asia giving a more bullish tone. Local buying interest was pegged in the low $190s cif Med but arbitrage options kept sellers scarce. Far East product is valued around $229 for May 16-31 delivery.
Fuel oil markets were stable with high sulphur markets on the tight side and low sulphur cargoes being offered into the Med from out of the region. Little business was done.
Prices were broadly unchanged with low sulphur cif offers talked in the $104 to $108 level. Lower low sulphur values in northern Europe were keeping offer levels down.
Transatlantic material was heard being firmly indicated into the Med, although the arbitrage looked tight, and the offers were above those coming from Europe, buyers said.

Asian interest was still drawing Russian gas oil eastwards amid few signs that the arb was likely to close. Traders said it was looking good into April for shipping product out of the region. Russian was pegged around high fob quotes +$2 although most barrels already have Far Eastern homes.
Non-Russian 0.2 percent material was talked around high fob quotes +$4.
